paragraphs: Rav Bibi. Rav Dimi: “It was Bibi’s Shabbat,” Rashi, his turn serving students; Ammi and Assi visited, Kelal Gadol 74, end of a. Heilprin’s copy reads Rav Bibi without a patronym. Jerusalem Talmud: Menachma in Bibi’s name. He asked Nachman, Bava Metzia 23b. Nachman: beer-drinker Bibi’s daughters need cosmetic paste, Shabbat 80b; Pesachim 43; Mo'ed Katan 9b. He recited before Nachman, Chagigah 22b; Nedarim 35b; Bava Batra 36b; Niddah 45a; Yevamot 100b. Yosef recited in Rabbi’s name; Bibi: “Do not listen: I told him in Adda bar Ahavah’s name,” Eruvin 75b. Kiddushin 81a: Bibi ate upstairs with Yosef. Rav Yosef and his wife descended while Bibi stayed upstairs, as Rashi explains. Rav Yosef ordered the ladder removed lest Bibi be alone with her, though husband in town, indeed at home: she was Bibi’s wedding companion and familiar with him. Semag, negative 126, cites the caution for familiar household visitors. Puzzling the codifiers mention only husband in town, not at home; see Shulchan Arukh, Even Ha'ezer 22. Pappa sat behind Bibi before Hamnuna, discussing Shimon’s reason, etc.; Pappa said, etc.; they laughed, etc.; Pappa further, etc., Niddah 27a. Rav Adda bar Ahavah’s host was a convert whose mother was an Israelite. He and Rav Bibi disputed who should hold public office. Rav Yosef assigned religious affairs to Rav Bibi, describing him as a great man, and municipal affairs to the convert. Rashi: charity collection/distribution, prophetic reading and translation versus walls, gates, springs. Shalshelet Hakkabbalah 33b writes: “Rav Bibi the convert, whose mother was an Israelite, disputed with Rav Adda bar Ahavah over public offices. They came before Rav Yosef, and he ruled: Rav Adda, who is a great man, should attend to, etc.; the convert to municipal affairs, etc.” See its corruption: Kiddushin 76b. Adda’s host—Rashi, householder—had eggs from festival to Shabbat and came before, etc., Beitzah 4a.
